title: Refactor crypto adapter layer and orchestrate JOSE/OpenSSL upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Multiple services depend on a mix of JOSE/JWT libraries (go-jose, python-jose, nimbus-jose) and an older OpenSSL base (2.1/3.0 forks across distro builds). This has caused recurring CVE remediation churn and inconsistent token validation behavior across language runtimes. We need a focused refactor to consolidate the platform's crypto adapter layer, upgrade JOSE/JWT libs to maintained versions, and standardize on OpenSSL 3.1+ builds where possible.

Scope:
- Introduce a thin, well-documented crypto-adapter abstraction (Go + Python + Java) to centralize signing/verification, JWK fetching/caching, and algorithm whitelisting.
- Upgrade JOSE/JWT libs: go-jose v3 -> v4 (or equivalent maintained fork), python-jose -> pyjwt 3.x, nimbus-jose-jwt -> 9.x.
- Migrate Linux packages/bundles to OpenSSL 3.1.x runtime builds and validate compatibility with musl/glibc images used in our runtime.
- Replace fragile SAML XML parsing usage (onelogin/python3-saml) with a hardened parser and stricter schema validation; add explicit entity/metadata caching window to reduce network dependency.
- Add CI security gates: dependency-scan job that fails builds for critical/high CVEs and a runtime smoke test for signing/verification parity.

Acceptance criteria:
- All services that perform JWT verification or signing call the new crypto-adapter API (shim allowed for staged migration).
- No failing unit/integration tests after upgrades; end-to-end auth flows pass in staging and canary clusters for 72h.
- Performance delta for token paths < 10% p95; any regressions must have mitigations (caching, batched JWK fetch).
- Security review completed and documented in the PR; release notes list CVE fixes.

Plan / Rollout:
1. Spike & matrix: build a compatibility matrix covering languages (Go, Python, Java) and OS images; record failing permutations. (Done: initial matrix attached).
2. Implement adapter interface and local shim in a single service (auth-proxy) behind a feature flag.
3. Upgrade JOSE/OpenSSL in auth-proxy, run perf regressions and security scans.
4. Gradual migration of downstream services via feature-flagged rollout and canary traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
5. Remove shims and old libs after 2 successful cycles and clean up build artifacts.

Risk & mitigations:
- FIPS/enterprise customers need FIPS-enabled OpenSSL builds: we will maintain a separate FIPS-compatible build profile and validate with security team.
- Transitive native deps (static linking) may increase image size: enforce a target increase < 5% and use strip/compression where needed.
- Token incompatibility: provide an opt-in compatibility mode that performs parallel verification with old and new libs and logs mismatches for triage.

Notes: See design doc for adapter API and example shim: https://go.confluence.internal/r/crypto-adapter-spike. Benchmarks and raw output: https://dashboards.internal/reports/crypto-upgrade-spike.
